name: Eman Zied
researchKeywords: spatial health inequalities, climate and health, built environment, heatwaves
bio:
Dr Eman Zied, PhD is a Research Fellow and geospatial data scientist affiliated with the Addressing Inequity in Health and Care Systems theme at NIHR ARC North East and North Cumbria.

Eman studies the interplay between social, spatial and health inequalities, including the spatial determinants of health and the effect of climate change on health outcomes. Her work examines the effects of built, natural and ambient environments on health. Her current programme of work examines spatial vulnerabilities to heatwaves through a health inequalities lens, with a view to developing interventions for local authorities and healthcare practitioners. She has previously worked on research projects focusing on the relationship between the environment and cognitive health, inequalities in health-related amenities on the high street and community pharmacy distribution in deprived areas.
